qt: to the Commission Gerald Hauser (PfE) Subject:

The EU-Morocco Agreement extending tariff preferences to agricultural products from Western Sahara has been provisionally applied since 4 October 2025, even though the European Parliament has not yet voted on its consent. On 4 October 2024, the CJEU ruled that the application of the EU-Morocco Agreement to Western Sahara was unlawful without the consent of its people. As Western Sahara is a separate territory from Morocco, the new agreement raises questions about compliance with CJEU rulings, parliamentary scrutiny and transparency. There are also concerns about food standards and a level playing field for EU producers. The fact that the agreement is being applied provisionally even before the European Parliament has given its consent is a critical issue. 1.

In light of the CJEU judgments of 4 October 2024 on Western Sahara, how does the Commission justify the provisional application of the agreement before the European Parliament has given its consent, and what specific measures are in place to ensure that the agreement complies with those judgments?

Why was the provisional application of the agreement permitted before the European Parliament had given its consent, and how does the Commission ensure that democratic scrutiny by the European Parliament is upheld?

What data does the Commission have on pesticide residues in agricultural products from Morocco and Western Sahara, in particular regarding residues of active substances that are not authorised as plant protection products in the EU?
